results.summary: This design is an early work-in-progress implementation of a low-power sensor interface for a multichannel acoustic emission detector. It contains four 12-bit pulse counters with overflow detection, an mm:ss real-time clock, and a parallel-in serial-out readout register controlled by a state machine. The counters accumulate pulses on four input channels and are read out serially after each RTC overflow or channel overflow. It is intended for low-power wake-up sensor interfaces, acoustic event detection, non-destructive testing, and particle counting.

results.summary: This project implements a lightweight machine-learning-based hardware anomaly detection engine for V2X packet data. It serially ingests 64-bit packets, extracts velocity and heading features, and runs a MAC-based inference core with ReLU activation and threshold scoring. The 8-bit threat score is output on uo_out, with done and interrupt flags on uio pins. The design is written in Verilog and can be tested by feeding serial packets and monitoring the outputs.
